official.deadline_note: The scholarship itself has no separate application deadline or form. Eligibility is tied to being admitted in the first admissions round for autumn semester 2027 (application period 16 October - 15 January at universityadmissions.se). Admitted students receive scholarship application instructions after the Notification of Selection Results (master's results published 1 April). Non-EU/EEA applicants must pay the 900 SEK application fee by 1 February and submit documents by 1 February. Newly admitted fee-paying students must pay the first tuition instalment by 10 May to keep the place.
official.application_cycle: Autumn semester 2027 - first admissions round, application period 16 October - 15 January
official.status_note: Current cycle is autumn semester 2027: first admission round application period 16 October - 15 January at universityadmissions.se; master's admission results published 1 April; scholarship offers notified by the end of April.
official.tuition_coverage_note: They cover partial or up to the full tuition fee but do not cover other expenses, such as living expenses.
benefits: They cover partial or up to the full tuition fee but do not cover other expenses, such as living expenses.

Students admitted to two-year programmes retain the scholarship for the second year if they successfully complete the first year of study and meet the progression criteria (minimum 22.5 credits a semester, minimum 45 credits an academic year).

For programme students, the waived tuition fee covers full-time studies on master's level, 60 credits per academic year, one Swedish or English language course, comprehensive insurance (FAS+ by Kammarkollegiet) and administrative services.

Fee-paying students are subject to the same services, rights and obligations as non-fee-paying students, such as study and career counselling, student health care, disability services, and access to library and university facilities.
eligibility: Students who have applied for an English-taught master's programme and meet all of the following conditions are eligible to apply for the Malmö University Master's Scholarship:
Applied in the first admissions round
Chose an English-taught master's programme at Malmö University as their first choice on University Admissions (ranked as number 1 of 4)
Were admitted to their first choice programme
Required to pay tuition fees for university studies in Sweden
Scholarships are offered to qualified master students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are required to pay tuition fees
requirements: Required to pay tuition fees for university studies in Sweden (citizenship outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland)

Meet the admission requirements of the chosen English-taught master's programme (most master's programmes require a bachelor's degree in a relevant field; entry requirements are listed on the programme's page in the online course catalogue)
Pay the application fee to University Admissions: applicants with citizenship from a non-EU/EEA country are required to pay an application fee of 900 SEK for the application to be processed

Meet the English language requirement: for most master's level programmes the equivalent of the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2 (some require English 5/Level 1 or English 7/Level 3 - check the programme page)
documents: Documentation of previous higher education studies: completed degree(s) and transcripts with courses and grades
Bachelor's Degree Certificate required for master's level studies
Documentation of English language skills (qualifying studies or internationally recognised test results)
The experience described in your CV is used in scholarship selection
Documentation of citizenship for fee status: EU/EEA and Swiss applicants must document their citizenship for the application to be processed
selection_criteria: Scholarship selection will be based on previous academic excellence, the experience described in your CV, and your ability to motivate social engagement through your chosen programme at Malmö University.
coverage: They cover partial or up to the full tuition fee but do not cover other expenses, such as living expenses.

The waived tuition fee covers full-time studies on master's level, 60 credits per academic year, one Swedish or English language course, comprehensive insurance (FAS+ by Kammarkollegiet) and administrative services.
application_method: Apply for one of our master's programmes through University Admissions as your first priority. Make sure to pay the application fee to University Admissions.
Admitted students will receive more information on how to apply for the scholarship after Notification of Selection Results.
Submit application documents by 1 February; the application fee and documents are processed by University Admissions.
official.application_route: Apply to an English-taught master's programme at Malmö University as first choice (rank 1 of 4) through universityadmissions.se in the first admissions round (16 October - 15 January), then follow the scholarship application instructions sent to admitted students after the Notification of Selection Results.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to students with citizenship outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are required to pay tuition fees for university studies in Sweden
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship targets non-EU/EEA and non-Swiss fee-paying international students; EU/EEA and Swiss citizens do not pay tuition fees and are not the intended group
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Must be an English-taught master's programme at Malmö University, chosen as first choice (ranked number 1 of 4) on University Admissions
official.duration: One-year and two-year master's programmes are offered; two-year students retain the scholarship for the second year if progression criteria are met (minimum 22.5 credits a semester, minimum 45 credits an academic year)
official.description: Each year, Malmö University offers a limited number of scholarships to qualified master students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland who are required to pay tuition fees. These scholarships are awarded on the basis of academic merit, experience and motivation and cover partial or up to the full tuition fee, but do not cover other expenses such as living expenses.
official.program_type: Tuition waiver scholarship for English-taught master's programmes
official.english_requirement: Master's studies require the equivalent of the Swedish upper secondary course English 6/English Level 2 (a few programmes require English 5/Level 1 or English 7/Level 3; the programme page states which). Published test scores include IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no section below 5.5, and TOEFL iBT total 90 (or 4.5 on the scale for results from 21 January 2026). The scholarship itself sets no separate English test requirement.

not_confirmed: Separate scholarship application deadline (none is published; timing follows the first admissions round)

Coverage wording, eligibility, selection criteria, notification timing and the first-round deadline (16 October - 15 January for autumn 2027) are confirmed verbatim; the official page publishes no SEK figure or percentage for the award itself (only 'partial or up to the full tuition fee'), so funding fields are null.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this as a tuition discount, not a full ride: the waiver covers part or all of the tuition fee, while housing, food, travel and the SEK application fee stay on your budget. The make-or-break move is ranking an English-taught Malmo master's as your first choice at universityadmissions.se and applying in the first admissions round (16 October - 15 January); ranking it lower or applying in the second round ends your eligibility outright. Since only a few scholarships are awarded each year on academic record, CV and social-engagement motivation, line up a fallback funding plan before the 10 May first tuition instalment deadline.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA fee-paying applicants with strong grades, a relevant CV and a genuine social-engagement motivation for one specific Malmo master's programme they are happy to rank first.
application_readiness_checklist: Register at universityadmissions.se early and submit between 16 October and 15 January with the target English-taught master's ranked as number 1 of 4.
Pay the 900 SEK application fee by 1 February as a non-EU/EEA citizen, otherwise the application is not processed at all.
Upload officially issued degree certificates, full transcripts and English documentation before the 1 February document deadline.
Prepare a CV and a concrete motivation for social engagement through the chosen programme, since these drive selection alongside academic excellence.
Secure a funding fallback for living costs before 15/16 April results and the 10 May first tuition instalment deadline.
common_rejection_risks: Ranking a Malmo master's as choice 2, 3 or 4 - the scholarship explicitly requires the programme ranked as number 1 of 4.
Applying in the second admissions round, which is in any case only open to EU/EEA and Swiss citizens and disqualifies non-EU/EEA applicants from this scholarship.
Missing the 1 February deadlines for the application fee or documents, which turns the application late and processed only at the university's discretion.
Failing to gain admission to the first-choice programme, since scholarship eligibility presupposes admission.
A generic CV or vague motivation, because selection weighs CV experience and social-engagement motivation, not just grades.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses including housing and food, travel to Sweden, the 900 SEK application fee, and any remaining tuition if only a partial waiver is awarded - the award covers tuition only.
document_audit: Documents must be officially issued; a letter from your school or university verifying English proficiency is not accepted unless you hold 60 ECTS in English-language instruction from a listed country.
Only IELTS Academic (not General Training or Indicator) is accepted, and results must be verifiable online via the TRF number or they are rejected.
Final-year bachelor's students must follow the special final-year documentation route if the degree is not yet complete.
Country-specific instructions decide exactly what you submit and how - check your country of study page rather than assuming a standard list.
The scholarship needs no separate upload; instructions arrive only after the Notification of Selection Results, so your admissions file must already be complete.
alerts: Only a few students are granted scholarships every year - the university itself tells applicants to plan tuition and living financing well in advance.
Unsuccessful applicants are not notified individually; no message by the end of April effectively means no scholarship.
Your admissions offer is conditional until the first tuition instalment is paid by the 10 May deadline, and missing any later instalment leads to suspension.
Tuition-fee-paying students must pay the first instalment before they can submit the residence permit application, so scholarship and permit timelines interlock.
The 7,000 SEK administrative refund deduction is waived only if you paid and were then granted a full scholarship.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Rank the programme first and apply via universityadmissions.se in the first round, pay the 900 SEK fee and upload documents by 1 February, receive master's results on 1 April, then follow the scholarship instructions sent to admitted students and hear the outcome by the end of April.
